reasoning: There were no regressions, but also no improvements: 18 of 20 tasks remained failures, so the previous guidance did not materially change performance. Its advice to save transformed results, preserve cache-key sequences, avoid “No planning needed” for updates, resolve affirmations, and use state-level attraction searches was repeatedly ignored: searches and filters were returned without saving, follow-up filters were skipped, affirmative amenity requests were treated as already complete, and AZ/GA were still mishandled as needing a city or as city names. The instruction to act only on the current turn may also have encouraged treating follow-ups in isolation; several failures required carrying forward an active trip plan, dates, cached entities, or proximity intent. A restaurant search added many unrequested criteria, and one call included budget=None and failed validation, so the revised guidance must make explicit that absent preferences are not defaults and unsupported criteria should be omitted without skipping supported work. The two stable successes support continuing to ask for genuinely missing required dates rather than guessing them; they do not justify asking again when the conversation already supplies the needed date or an unambiguous duration.
slow_update_content:
Treat follow-ups as part of the active plan: use the full conversation to carry forward still-valid routes, cities, dates, durations, entities, and requested domains, and change only what the user has changed. A date or duration in a later message can complete an earlier request; for an explicit number of nights, calculate checkout with adjust_date, then perform every now-complete requested search in the same turn. Ask once only for inputs that are still genuinely missing.

Complete each workflow end to end before returning code. Retrieve compatible cached results as a separate call and assign them; assign each search, filter, and nearest result; perform all dependent steps; and save every new search, transformation, or nearest result under the appropriate base or next numbered cache key. A bare search, cache read, or filter call is incomplete. For example, a follow-up filter must retrieve the current result, assign the filtered output, and save it as the next result in that chain. If a new criterion applies to multiple active result sets, such as a budget cap on both flight legs, filter and save each relevant set.

Do not say “No planning needed” while any requested action remains. If a request includes both supported and unsupported preferences, execute the supported portion and omit only the unsupported criterion. Pass only preferences explicitly stated or clearly inherited from the active request: do not infer defaults, add unrequested boolean options, pass false flags merely because a preference was not mentioned, or include None-valued arguments.

Interpret locations by their kind: when attraction search supports state, pass a supplied state abbreviation in state (for example, AZ as state="AZ" or GA as state="GA"), not as a city, and do not ask for a city. When the user asks for something near a named hotel or attraction, resolve that place as the anchor entity from the conversation—not as a neighborhood—ensure compatible results exist for both sides, run search_nearest, and save its result using the requested organizing domain.
update_target: Address longitudinal regressions and persistent failures observed across adjacent epochs.
